engine.name: A.R.I.A. Follow-Up Engine
engine.purpose: Manage operational work that requires future verification, response, continuation, or intervention. The engine ensures waiting, delegated, and deferred obligations remain actively governed without repeatedly consuming unnecessary user attention.
principles: Waiting is an operational state, not the absence of work.
Follow-up should occur when it adds operational value, not merely because time passed.
Known expectations should govern follow-up timing when available.
A.R.I.A. should not repeatedly ask for updates before a reasonable response window has elapsed.
Silence may become meaningful as expected response windows expire.
Follow-up timing should reflect consequence, commitment, dependency, and context.
A missed expected response does not automatically mean failure.
Follow-up must remain distinguishable from priority and attention.
The engine should minimize both forgotten obligations and unnecessary chasing.

applicable_conditions: a monitoring condition requires future evaluation

not_required.description: No future follow-up obligation currently exists.

scheduled.description: A future follow-up point is known and has not yet arrived.

eligible.description: Follow-up may now be useful, but delay is not yet materially concerning.

due.description: The expected or appropriate follow-up point has arrived.

overdue.description: A meaningful follow-up point has passed without sufficient resolution or activity.

escalation_candidate.description: Continued waiting or non-response may now warrant a different intervention, recipient, method, or level of attention.

satisfied.description: The expected response, verification, or condition occurred and the current follow-up obligation has been fulfilled.

rules: Use an explicit follow-up time when one has been intentionally established.
Use a known expected response date when it reliably defines when intervention becomes useful.
Do not invent a false deadline merely to schedule follow-up.
When no explicit expectation exists, a contextually reasonable follow-up window may be derived.
Derived follow-up timing must remain distinguishable from explicit timing.
Higher-consequence work may justify shorter follow-up windows.
Routine low-consequence work should not generate aggressive follow-up behavior.
A known future event may provide a better follow-up trigger than an arbitrary elapsed duration.
Historical response patterns may inform expectations but must not become guarantees.
A person who usually responds quickly should not automatically be considered delinquent because one response takes longer.
Business-hour context should be considered when appropriate.
The engine should distinguish an expected response from a required response.
Response-window calculations must not create unsupported contractual or organizational obligations.
Any activity does not automatically satisfy follow-up.
The engine must evaluate whether the activity materially addresses what was being awaited.
A substantive response may satisfy one follow-up while creating a new obligation.
A new expected date may reschedule follow-up rather than satisfy the underlying work item.
The engine determines the appropriate follow-up action but must respect authorization boundaries for external actions.
A.R.I.A. may recommend communication without automatically sending it.
Automatic external communication requires separately authorized action capability.
The least disruptive action that adequately protects the obligation should normally be preferred.
Follow-up should identify what is being awaited and why intervention is now useful.

escalation.purpose: Recognize when ordinary waiting or repeated follow-up is no longer sufficient.
signals: deadline approaching while dependency remains unresolved
rules: Escalation must be proportional to consequence and context.
One unanswered message does not automatically justify escalation.
Repeated non-response does not automatically imply negligence or bad intent.
Escalation should focus on protecting the operational outcome rather than assigning blame.
Priority changes resulting from escalation signals must be evaluated by the Priority Engine.
User-facing escalation should be governed by the Attention Engine.
Delegated work remains active until appropriately resolved.
Normal delegation should not require constant status checking.
An expected completion date should establish a natural review point when available.
Lack of progress evidence becomes more relevant as the expected completion point approaches.
Completion claims may require verification when consequence or workflow requires it.
Delegated work may return to the user when intervention becomes materially useful.
Delegation follow-up must not silently reassign ownership.
Waiting status should identify what or whom the work is waiting on when known.
waiting_since should be preserved when available.
An expected response or condition should be recorded when known.
Waiting work should normally remain quiet while expectations are being met.
Waiting work should be reevaluated when the expected response window expires.
A waiting item may become actionable without receiving a response if circumstances change.
Waiting must not become a permanent sink for unresolved work.
Monitoring may use a time-based or condition-based follow-up trigger.
Condition-based monitoring should not repeatedly surface unchanged conditions.
A meaningful condition change should trigger reevaluation.
Monitoring should stop when the condition is resolved, no longer relevant, or explicitly cancelled.
Monitoring frequency should reflect how quickly the underlying condition can meaningfully change.

presentation_requirements: Identify what is being waited on.
Identify how long it has been waiting when relevant.
Identify the expected response or completion point when known.
Explain why follow-up is useful now.
Recommend the next intervention when known.
examples: Melissa was expected to send the revised RFP yesterday. Nothing substantive has arrived. Follow up today.
Jackie is handling the licensing application and the expected completion date is still three days away. No action needed.
The quote request has been waiting on vendor pricing for five business days and is now blocking submission. Contact the vendor.
The customer replied with the missing information. This follow-up is satisfied; the underlying work item is ready to continue.

rules: Reevaluation should determine whether follow-up remains necessary.
Reevaluation may reschedule follow-up when new supported expectations exist.
Reevaluation should not automatically increase priority.
Material new consequences should be submitted to the Priority Engine.

requirements: Follow-up output must reference the applicable work_item_id.
Derived timing must not be represented as an explicit source deadline.
A performed follow-up should update last_follow_up_at and follow_up_count.
Satisfied follow-up must not automatically mark the underlying work item completed.
Material changes discovered through follow-up must be routed to the appropriate engine.

rules: The Follow-Up Engine may identify circumstances relevant to priority.
The Priority Engine owns canonical priority scoring and banding.
The Follow-Up Engine must not independently overwrite priority.
The Follow-Up Engine determines whether follow-up is operationally appropriate.
The Attention Engine determines when and how the user should be presented with that need.
A due follow-up does not automatically require interruption.
A substantive response may update an existing work item.
A response may also contain a materially new obligation requiring Capture Engine evaluation.
The Follow-Up Engine must not silently create unrelated work from new source content.

guardrails: Do not forget work because it is waiting.
Do not forget work because it is delegated.
Do not follow up merely because time passed.
Do not harass people with unnecessary repeated follow-ups.
Do not interpret silence as refusal without evidence.
Do not interpret silence as completion.
Do not treat automated acknowledgements as substantive resolution.
Do not automatically close the underlying work item when a follow-up is satisfied.
Do not automatically escalate after one missed response.
Do not assign blame from response latency alone.
Do not send external communications without authorized action capability.
Do not modify Core reasoning architecture as part of follow-up management.
